title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a chain of equivalent (or one-way implied) statements about cycles. It continues the previous page, which listed analogous statements for A^*(X)^Q. In the notation, A^i(X)^a means codimension-i cycles that are algebraically equivalent to zero, modulo some adequate equivalence. The symbol ~_τ is that equivalence; it could be rational equivalence modulo torsion, or a relation Grothendieck is trying to define. The word read as "univ" in the transcription looks in the image like "nul" (zero), underlined.

The statements, in modern language:
- 1°) The intersection product A^i(X)^a × A^j(X)^a → A^{i+j}(X) is zero.
- 1° bis) Equivalently, the external product A^i(X)^a × A^j(Y)^a → A^{i+j}(X×Y) is zero. The two forms pass into each other by pulling back along the diagonal and by pulling back from the factors.
- 2°) This implies the special case of 0-cycles: A_0(X)^a × A_0(Y)^a → A_0(X×Y) is zero.
- 2° bis) It is enough to take X = Y (replace X and Y by X⊔Y or X×Y).
- 3°) Concrete form: for points a, x ∈ X and b, y ∈ Y, the cycle (x,y) − (x,b) − (a,y) + (a,b) ~_τ 0. Here (x)−(a) and (y)−(b) generate the algebraically trivial 0-cycles of degree 0 when X and Y are connected.
- 3° bis) The same with X = Y; the notation 'K^{ij}' is unclear.
- A crossed-out line 'A_0(X)^τ → Alb(X)' precedes the next step.
- 4°) For an abelian variety A and x, y ∈ A: (x+y) − (x) − (y) + (0) ~_τ 0. That is, x ↦ (x) − (0) is a group homomorphism A → A_0(A)^τ, and it is surjective (marked with '!').
- 4° bis) Equivalently, the summation (Albanese) map A_0(A)^a → A is an isomorphism, with the map of 4° as its inverse.
- 5°) For every (smooth projective) X, the Albanese map A_0(X)^a → Alb(X) is an isomorphism. A marginal parenthesis, perhaps 'générique…' or 'conjectural', is unclear.
- 6°) For X and Y, the map A_0(X×Y)^a → A_0(X)^a × A_0(Y)^a is bijective; 6° bis is the same with X = Y.

What the chain says: 'products of algebraically trivial cycles vanish' is equivalent to 'the Albanese kernel T(X) on 0-cycles vanishes', and to 'Alb is compatible with products'. The mechanism is the classical fact that the kernel of CH_0(A)_0 → A is the square I^{*2} of the augmentation ideal for the Pontryagin product, generated by the elements (x+y)−(x)−(y)+(0). It is also used that A_0(X)^a maps onto A_0(Alb X)^a via X → Alb(X).

Purpose: in notes on the standard conjectures, Grothendieck is testing which equivalence relations (or which base fields) make algebraically trivial cycles behave like a square-zero ideal, so that the 0-cycle part reduces exactly to the Albanese variety.
errors: For rational equivalence over C, statements 4°, 5° and 6° are false: by Mumford (1969), T(X) is huge when p_g > 0. The chain is therefore only consistent as (i) a list of equivalent conditions, (ii) a statement about a coarser relation τ, or (iii) a statement over special fields such as Q-bar or F_p-bar, where Bloch–Beilinson-type conjectures predict it after tensoring with Q. The page does not say which; the marginal word next to 5° and 6° may be a hedge such as 'conjectural'.

Several implications are written as ⇔ although only one direction is immediate. For example, 2° ⇒ 1° (0-cycles controlling all codimensions) is not justified on the page, and 1° bis ⇒ 2° is drawn as a single arrow.
The implication 4° bis ⇒ 5° needs that the kernel of A_0(X)^a → A_0(Alb X)^a vanishes modulo τ. This is not obvious and is not argued; it is presumably meant to follow from 6° and 3°.

ideas.what: Vanishing of the intersection or external product of algebraically trivial cycles, as a condition equivalent to triviality of the Albanese kernel on 0-cycles
ideas.modern_name: Bloch–Beilinson filtration property F^1·F^1 ⊂ F^2, with F^2 CH_0 = T(X); Bloch's conjecture / Beilinson's conjecture over Q-bar that products of homologically trivial cycles vanish ⊗Q
ideas.usually_credited_to: S. Bloch (1970s–1980), A. Beilinson (1980s), J. Murre (1990s)

ideas.what: (x+y)−(x)−(y)+(0) generates the kernel of the Albanese map on 0-cycles of an abelian variety
ideas.modern_name: Pontryagin augmentation ideal I^{*2} = ker(CH_0(A)_0 → A)

ideas.what: Albanese compatible with products: A_0(X×Y)^a ≅ A_0(X)^a × A_0(Y)^a after quotienting by τ
ideas.modern_name: Alb(X×Y) = Alb X × Alb Y; motivic (Murre) decomposition of the Albanese part h_1

missed.claim: Grothendieck writes down, as a chain of equivalences, that 'products of algebraically trivial cycles vanish' (all codimensions) is equivalent to 'the Albanese map on 0-cycles is an isomorphism'. This anticipates the Bloch–Beilinson philosophy, in which F^1·F^1 ⊂ F^2 and F^2 CH_0 is the Albanese kernel, as well as Beilinson's prediction that over Q-bar such products vanish ⊗Q.
missed.quote: A^i(X)^a × A^j(X)^a → A^{i+j}(X)^a nul ... ⇔ ... A_0(X)^a → Alb ... isom
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an early, pre-Bloch formulation linking the multiplicative structure of algebraically trivial cycles to the Albanese kernel. It is of historical interest, but the mathematics has since been developed independently.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is mostly elementary reformulation, but it shows Grothendieck around 1965–71 explicitly relating vanishing of products of algebraically trivial cycles to the Albanese kernel. That anticipates themes later credited to Bloch and Beilinson. The status of the claims (conjecture, definition of τ, or the base field) is unclear, which limits the significance.
transcription_corrections: 'univ' after each of 1°, 1° bis, 2°, 2° bis is more likely 'nul' (underlined): the product maps are asserted to be zero.
In 3°, '~_τ 0' is correct; the condition is 'a, x ∈ X, b, y ∈ Y'.
In 5°, the target should be read as 'Alb(X)', not 'Alb(A)'.
In 4°, the bracketed remark reads roughly 'et c'est surjectif !'.
